description: data-ref value absent from the entry's refs[] array
reason: refs[] is dropped from truth (B7, body model §5) and the reference index is derived at compile from the <cite ref> tags; entry.schema.json sets additionalProperties:false with no refs property. This pattern is the stated reason for the drop — §5 measures 31% of inline citations missing from refs — so it cannot exist in a representation that has no refs array.

description: raw space before the href disambiguator (/Jastrow,_מוּר I.1)
reason: Same D7 reasoning: the unencoded space sits in the href only. All 9,804 spaced-href anchors carry a data-ref whose disambiguator is plain text ("Jastrow, מוּר IV 1"), which is what internal rid resolution reads; no URL survives the transform to carry the space.

description: Jerusalem Talmud href missing its leading slash
reason: href strings are not stored in v2 (D7, body model §2: "no URLs are stored" — both destinations derive at compile from the <cite ref> value). All 7,679 slash-less anchors carry a well-formed data-ref ("Jerusalem Talmud Nedarim 5:6:3"), so the stored ref value is already correct; the defect dies with the href.

description: bare RTL Hebrew in definition text with no dir=rtl wrapper
Jastrow data-ref whose headword skeleton is absent from the corpus
reason: SURVIVES — rule needed (B10: rid values must resolve to an existing entry). COUNT UNRELIABLE: corpusCount 2572 was not reproduced by any comparison rule. Re-measured over all Jastrow-targeted anchors: 34 by consonantal-skeleton family (link-anomalies.ts skeleton()), 81 anchors / 79 entries by exact vocalized headword with homograph stripped (agreeing with the parent spec's D8 "88 do not" and upstream-issues register #11), 7,611 by raw string equality. Phase 2 must pin the comparison rule and re-count before sizing the transform; see docs/v2/pattern-triage.md.

description: duplicate anchor wrap in non-sense fields (language_reference etc.)
unlinked v. <span dir=rtl> cross-references the linker never anchored
empty string slot in plural_form array
reason: plural_form is not a v2 field: BodyEntry has no such property and entry.schema.json (additionalProperties:false) forbids it; B2 keeps plural phrases as gloss prose, and rejoin.ts concatenates only morphology + language_code + language_reference + sense-1 text, never plural_form. 10,343 of 10,455 non-empty values already locate in their own entry body, so the array is a dropped upstream extraction and its empty slots reach nothing. Reopens if the rejoin is ever taught to append plural_form with a separator: 701 of the 703 entries hold sibling non-empty values, so only separator-free concatenation keeps the empty slot invisible.

description: gender label (f., m.) left in the definition instead of a morphology field
reason: v2 has no morphology field to be "left out of": B2 rejoins the marker into the gloss deliberately, so a marker already in the definition is in its correct v2 place (710 measured entries, 709 with empty language_reference, so the rejoin order is unaffected). grammar.gender is a separate typed index seeded from the 13,162 content.morphology markers; extending that seeding is post-migration enrichment under the index↔text lint, not a text transform.

description: "Targ. II Esth." (Targum Sheni) is unlinked in all 384 occurrences while Targ. Esth. and Targ. II Chr. link normally

Hab." - 37 occurrences, inside an anchor 0 times - links to Habakkuk itself. PROBE NOTE: the first consolidation pass recorded this as non-reproducing because its probe required the display INSIDE the anchor to start with "Targ."; in every instance "Targ." sits OUTSIDE the anchor and only the book+chapter is linked (D00892: Targ. Hab. II, 19). Any pattern whose defining text sits outside the anchor is invisible to a display-side probe.
